# Lab 24.6: Enable & Analyze VPC Flow Logs

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on VPC Flow Logs for a subnet, generate traffic, and find who talked to whom.

## Steps

1. **Enable flow logs on a subnet** with full sampling for the lab.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute networks subnets update default --region=us-central1 \
  --enable-flow-logs \
  --logging-aggregation-interval=interval-5-sec \
  --logging-flow-sampling=1.0 \
  --logging-metadata=include-all</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Create two VMs and generate traffic.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances create flow-a flow-b --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-micro
gcloud compute ssh flow-a --zone=us-central1-a \
  --command="ping -c 5 $(gcloud compute instances describe flow-b --zone=us-central1-a --format='value(networkInterfaces[0].networkIP)'); curl -s -o /dev/null https://www.google.com"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Query the flow logs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • TEXT
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">resource.type="gce_subnetwork"
log_id("compute.googleapis.com/vpc_flows")
jsonPayload.src_instance.vm_name="flow-a"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Each entry shows source and destination IPs, ports, protocol, bytes and VM names.

4. **Use Flow Analyzer.** Go to **Network Intelligence → Flow Analyzer**. Group traffic by source and destination to see the top talkers.

5. **Think about cost.** For production, lower the sampling, for example `0.5`, and use a longer interval.

6. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances delete flow-a flow-b --zone=us-central1-a --quiet
gcloud compute networks subnets update default --region=us-central1 --no-enable-flow-logs</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Captured | Metadata of flows, no payload |
| Granularity | Per subnet, with sampling |
| Uses | Forensics, exfiltration checks, cost |
| Tool | Flow Analyzer for quick exploration |
